task.description: Measured with cargo tree: every consumer already reaches miter-engine transitively through chalkline-core (dado 434 crates via chalkline, batten 434, joiner 483, rabbet 591; engine subtree 165). So repointing dado/batten to a lighter crate removes nothing - MTR-10 as scoped has zero dependency and zero compile-time effect and should be rescoped or closed. The edge worth cutting is chalkline-core's use of inspect_workspace: the whole inventory module references no sibling module and none of redb, sqlparser, hcl, dockerfile-parser, serde_yaml, globset or rayon, yet it lives in the crate that pulls all eight. Cheapest lever is feature gating - make storage, the declarative parsers and rayon non-default features so a consumer can take miter-engine with default-features = false plus inventory and language - which needs no new crates; extracting miter-inventory is the cleaner but larger alternative.
task.title: Feature gate miter-engine's heavy subsystems so inventory-only consumers stop linking the analysis stack
